description: The USGS has produced nationwide water-use data since 1950, giving comparable county, state and national estimates of how much water is withdrawn and consumed and for what purpose. It now publishes eight categories: public supply, irrigation, thermoelectric power, domestic self-supply, industrial, mining, livestock and aquaculture, with withdrawals from surface water and groundwater and consumptive use. Monthly estimates for 2000 to 2020 cover public supply and irrigation, and thermoelectric power from 2009, through the National Water Availability Data Companion, while 2020 estimates for the other five categories and all historic estimates are released on ScienceBase, and the page links the original Water Use Circulars. The USGS is moving to machine learning models to estimate withdrawals and consumptive use. Coverage is the United States. Access is free as data releases, and USGS content is public domain. Caveats: methods and category definitions have changed over time, so long series need care. Simulation uses: demand inputs for water supply, irrigation and thermoelectric cooling models and drought planning. Related records: USGS public supply water use reanalysis (data-usgs-public-supply-water-use-reanalysis-huc12) and monthly irrigation water use (data-usgs-monthly-irrigation-water-use-huc12-2015).
